title: Uniform truncation window for proper classical direct images after base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Suppose $e\geq0$ bounds the dimensions of all fibres after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For any scheme map $S\to Y$, write $f_S:X_S=X\times_YS\to S$. In the ordinary constant-$A$ unbounded pro-étale derived categories, let $J\in D(X_S,A)$ have classical cohomology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-pe-classical-definition]. For integers $m,N$ with $N<m-2e-1$, the canonical truncation map induces a natural isomorphism of sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$
$$\mathcal H^mRf_{S,*}J\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^mRf_{S,*}\tau_{\geq N}J.$$
Use total K-injective direct image and good truncations [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] [def-kun-truncations]. The same $e$ and inequality work for every $S$.

source.place: Étale statements, both sides depend on a bounded-below truncation; old split steps 9–10

proof.text: Fix $S\to Y$ and an affine weakly contractible $W\to S$. Put $Z=X_S\times_SW=X\times_YW$ and $r:Z\to X_S$. Base change of site objects [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] makes $r$ an object of $(X_S)_{\mathrm{proét}}$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $f_S$ is proper. Every further base change is also a base change of $f$, so has the same fibre bound $e$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-neighborhood-vanishing] to $f_S,W$: $H^qR\Gamma(Z,H[0])=0$ for every classical $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $Z$ and $q>2e$.

source.place: Étale statements: uniform bound after arbitrary base change

proof.text: Write $L=r^*J$. The inverse-image comparison in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and exactness of all its inverse images imply that $L$ has classical cohomology: apply $r^*\nu_{X_S}^*\cong\nu_Z^*r_{\mathrm{ét}}^*$ to each cohomology sheaf, using [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. This holds for every discrete commutative $A$. By [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], $r^*$ is exact restriction with its constant-$A$ action. Applying it to the kernels and cokernels in [def-kun-truncations] identifies $r^*\tau_{\geq N}J$ with $\tau_{\geq N}L$, including their canonical maps.

source.place: Transfer: classical restriction and canonical truncation

proof.text: Evaluation at $W$ is exact by [det-proper-heart-continuity-sections]. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $J$ as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives $(f_{S,*}I)(W)=I(Z)$ termwise. By [lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization], the latter computes derived sections of the localized restriction. The site and constant coefficient identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], together with the restriction identification in step 2, makes this $R\Gamma(Z,L)$. Exact evaluation therefore identifies $(\mathcal H^mRf_{S,*}J)(W)$ with $H^mR\Gamma(Z,L)$. These are identities on resolution maps followed by natural restriction isomorphisms, hence are natural in $J$ and apply to $J\to\tau_{\geq N}J$.

source.place: Transfer: evaluate total direct image on weakly contractible objects

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation] on the scheme $Z$, with its terminal site object and bound $2e$. Step 1 verifies its vanishing hypothesis for ALL classical sheaves, and step 2 verifies classicality of $L$. The given inequality is exactly $N<m-(2e)-1$. Thus $H^mR\Gamma(Z,L)\to H^mR\Gamma(Z,\tau_{\geq N}L)$ is invertible. Step 3 identifies this with evaluation of the asserted sheaf map. Since $W$ was arbitrary, clause (3) of [det-pe-sections-conservative] proves that map is an isomorphism. Naturality follows from the canonical maps just used; $S$ was arbitrary and the bound never changed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-b60a17972 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS; no changes made. Shape: the item's statement and stmt_deps are identical to the side-live unsplit version, nothing is weakened. There is no repair note, nothing is on the drop list, no SGA is cited, and every cited id exists and is unmerged with proof_deps equal to the union of the step uses. Step 1: det-pe-topos-functoriality makes r:Z=X_S×_S W→X_S a site object, lem-pc-proper-base-change(1) makes f_S proper, and the bound e passes to f_S. Step 2: the first clause of sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison together with det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules shows r^*J is classical; lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction(3) is A-linear exact restriction, so it commutes with def-kun-truncations. Step 3: exact Γ(W,−) (det-proper-heart-continuity-sections), (f_*I)(W)=I(Z) from def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, the statement of lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization (unbounded K allowed) and lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization; the identities are natural on resolutions. Step 4: det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation(2) is applied on Z at the terminal object with bound 2e, and N<m−2e−1 matches exactly; det-pe-sections-conservative(3) then gives the sheaf isomorphism. New node: self-contained and statement-only, with all four search kinds recorded. It is true: finite A makes the sheaves torsion, Stacks 095U (etale-cohomology.tex l.18786, no Noetherian or invertibility hypothesis) gives the étale vanishing, the qcqs bounded-below comparison moves it to pro-étale, and exact Γ on the affine weakly contractible V gives the absolute bound. Checked A=0, Z empty, e=0 and non-Noetherian V. It is not a restatement of the item and not a duplicate: lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound is the relative étale part only, and det-proper-heart-bound-torsion covers only lisse lattices over a field. I accept the 13 tool_uses as generic pro-étale and site tools; three of them are definitions, which is harmless and advisory only.
